title: Shade for Memphis
prompt: Design a small public shelter that would make a hot Memphis afternoon feel noticeably better.

title: Room for the River
prompt: Make a riverfront pavilion that frames the water without turning its back on the city.

rules.label: Keep it to 18 parts or fewer

title: The Public Porch
prompt: Design a place that is not quite inside and not quite outside—a generous threshold for people to gather.

bonus.label: Bonus: give the porch some shade

title: Memphis After Dark
prompt: Design a small public building whose identity becomes stronger after sunset.

title: Tiny Gallery
prompt: Make a one-room gallery where the entrance, daylight, and one memorable spatial gesture do most of the work.

bonus.label: Bonus: use an arch as the main gesture

title: Break the Rhythm
prompt: Create a facade with a strong repeated order, then break that order exactly where something important happens.

bonus.label: Bonus: rotate one part to break the order

title: Civic Edge
prompt: Design a small civic building that feels public and welcoming without relying on a perfectly symmetrical facade.

bonus.label: Bonus: make the site feel civic too

title: Life in the Courtyard
prompt: Build around an outdoor room. The empty middle should feel as intentional as the building masses around it.

rules.label: Put at least 2 trees in the composition

bonus.label: Bonus: use the campus lawn scene

title: Glass Stack
prompt: Make a vertical building with a readable base, middle, and top using repetition rather than detail overload.

bonus.label: Bonus: keep the whole tower under 22 parts

title: Heavy / Light
prompt: Make the bottom feel grounded and heavy while the top feels unexpectedly light.

rules.label: Keep the palette to 4 colors or fewer

bonus.label: Bonus: open the upper mass with windows

title: Landscape First
prompt: Make the landscape feel like the first design move, not the decoration added at the end.

rules.label: Use no more than 3 building masses

bonus.label: Bonus: use the campus lawn scene

title: One Arch Rules Everything
prompt: Start with one arch and make every other move support, frame, repeat, or contrast it.

bonus.label: Bonus: frame the arch with columns

title: Three-Color Discipline
prompt: Build a complete composition using exactly three colors. Make hierarchy come from form, not extra decoration.

bonus.label: Bonus: resolve it in 16 parts or fewer

title: Read It as a Silhouette
prompt: Design a building whose massing would still be recognizable if every material and color disappeared.

bonus.label: Bonus: give the skyline a roof move

title: A Tower That Says Hello
prompt: Make a tall building whose base feels genuinely welcoming instead of simply stopping at the ground.

rules.label: Create at least 2 points of entry
Use at least 2 columns at the base

bonus.label: Bonus: soften the base with landscape

title: Quiet Building
prompt: Design something calm enough that one unusual move becomes impossible to ignore.

rules.label: Use at least 1 obvious rotated move

bonus.label: Bonus: add only the openings you really need

title: Make an Arcade
prompt: Create a repeated covered edge that could become a walkway, market, gallery, or public threshold.

bonus.label: Bonus: connect the arcade to an entrance

title: Campus Hangout
prompt: Design a small campus place that feels open enough to wander into and structured enough to stay awhile.

bonus.label: Bonus: make a strong shade canopy
